/*
COPY runner/launch.c /tmp/launch.c
RUN gcc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -o /usr/local/bin/sterra-launch /tmp/launch.c

FROM ${NODE_IMAGE} AS runner
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="1.1.0"
ENV NODE_ENV=production STERRACODE_MODE=docker STERRACODE_WORKSPACE_DIR=/workspaces RUNNER_STATE_DIR=/runner-state RUNNER_CACHE_DIR=/package-cache RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE_DIR=/tool-cache RUNNER_TEMP_DIR=/runs RUNNER_LAUNCHER=/usr/local/bin/sterra-launch STERRACODE_RUNNER_SECRET_FILE=/run/secrets/runner_key DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bash ca-certificates gpg curl xz-utils procps tar git findutils && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && groupadd --gid 10001 sterracode && useradd --uid 10002 --gid 10001 --no-create-home sterra-run \
    && mkdir -p /opt/sterracode
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=launcher /usr/local/bin/sterra-launch /usr/local/bin/sterra-launch
COPY runner ./runner
COPY server ./server
COPY shared ./shared
COPY package.json ./
EXPOSE 3001
CMD ["node", "runner/index.js"]

# Nachvollziehbare i18n-Inventarzuordnung

Dieser Bericht ergänzt den unveränderten Auditor. Er setzt keine `config.exceptions`, akzeptiert keine Befunde und behauptet keine statische Vollständigkeit dynamischen Codes. Die Referenzen verweisen auf Literal-IDs und originale Befundfingerprints in den drei Eingabedateien. **Textgleichheit mit einem Katalog ist kein Zuordnungskriterium.**

Erneuter Aufruf nach dem finalen Audit: `node scripts/review-i18n.mjs`. Die Ausgabe ist bei gleichen Eingaben und Quellen deterministisch. Quellhashabweichungen bleiben sichtbar und dürfen nicht als abgeschlossene aktuelle Quellprüfung ausgegeben werden.

## Ergebnis

-  Literalquellen,  Befunde und  einzeln referenzierte dynamische Grenzen.
-  Literalquellen ohne hinreichenden Herkunftsbeleg.
-  physische Quellen mit verändertem/fehlendem Quellhash gegenüber dem Audit.
- Auditorannahmen, offene Befunde und angenommene Ausnahmen bleiben unverändert; akzeptierte Auditbefunde: .

| Kategorie | Literale | Befunde |
| --- | ---: | ---: |

| Ungeklärt |  |  |

## Belegarten

Gebundene Fallbacks benötigen einen nachprüfbaren AST-Coowner: `new AppError/RunnerError(message, status, code, {messageKey, params})`, ein Objekt mit eigenem Textfeld und zugehörigem Descriptorschlüssel oder benachbarte Zuweisungen an dasselbe Objekt im selben Block. HTML verwendet die tatsächlichen `data-i18n`-/Attributbindungen. Statische technische Rollen, Vergleichswerte und explizite Vertragsfelder werden getrennt ausgewiesen. Produktkataloge werden anhand ihres Ressourcenpfads erfasst, nicht anhand gleicher Formulierungen.

Dynamische Grenzen behalten pro Senke Quelldatei, Zeile, Ausgabebeschreibung, Ursachenliste, Quellausschnitt und referenzierten Herkunftsvertrag. `reviewed-runtime-contract` bedeutet eine überprüfte Laufzeitgrenze, keinen statischen Beweis aller möglichen Werte. Die Grenzen stehen vollständig in [zuordnung.json](zuordnung.json). Generische UI-/API-Helfer dürfen sowohl übersetzte Anwendungstexte als auch Originaldaten transportieren.

Die Inhalts-/Tutorverträge stehen in [INHALTE.md](INHALTE.md), die Server-/Runnerverbraucher in [SERVER-TEXTFLUESSE.md](SERVER-TEXTFLUESSE.md). Interne Prompt-/Snapshot-/Toolschemata werden nicht nachträglich in Modellhistorien übersetzt. Tests und optionale Betreiberstufe sind ausdrücklich getrennte Kategorien, keine stillen Ausnahmen.

## Ungeklärte Quellen

Die folgende Liste ist ein Arbeitsauftrag, keine pauschale Baseline. Für jede Stelle fehlt noch ein hinreichender Herkunfts-/Ausgabebeleg. Alle Einträge stehen mit vollständiger Literalreferenz im JSON.

*
 * Pass capping for the tool loop without the SDK's `maxPredictionRounds`.
 *
 * `act({ maxPredictionRounds: N })` runs its Nth round with tools DISABLED so
 * the model is forced to answer. A model still mid-task then writes its tool
 * call as plain text in its native syntax (`<tool_call><function=...>`),
 * which streams into the chat as content and is never executed; the next
 * pass repeats the call for real. Every capped pass paid that wasted,
 * visible round.
 *
 * Instead, the handler passes no round limit and ends a pass by aborting
 * act()'s signal at the end of the last allowed round — after that round's
 * assistant message and tool results were emitted — so the SDK's loop stops
 * before starting another prediction. A pass is also ended early when the
 * grown history would no longer fit the next request, so mid-task
 * compaction can run before the engine rejects the prompt.
 *
 * Pure: no SDK imports, testable with plain AbortControllers.

*

 * approximation and an early pass end costs one cheap budget check, while
 * an engine 400 kills the turn.

 * everything generated since, plus the tool definitions — still leaves the
 * reply reserve inside the window. The between-pass fit check reserves a
 * static allowance per round; this is the dynamic check against what a
 * reasoning-heavy model actually produced (thousands of tokens of reasoning
 * per round stay in the history within a pass).

 * "<reasoning>__LM_STUDIO_INTERNAL_LSEP_SYNTHETIC_REASONING_END_<hex>__<content>",
 * one such pair per tool round in a single text: the app parses the think
 * tags we stream for display, then flattens each round back to plain text
 * with a synthetic end-of-reasoning marker, and ChatMessage.getText() hands
 * that whole string back as history. Left in place, the reasoning is re-sent
 * as content and the model learns to echo the marker itself (observed on
 * qwen3.8-27b). There is no start marker, so the content of a round cannot
 * be told apart from the next round's reasoning: only what follows the last
 * marker is kept, which is the reply's final visible text.

literals.staticText:
You are a faithful context compressor for an ongoing conversation between a user and an AI assistant. Summarize the conversation excerpt you are given into a dense, structured summary that preserves EVERYTHING needed to continue the task seamlessly, whatever kind of task it is (coding, research, writing, planning, or anything else).

Structure the summary with these sections, and omit any section that has nothing to report:
- Goal & task type: what the user is trying to achieve.
- Decisions & rationale: choices made and why.
- Constraints & preferences: requirements and preferences the user stated.
- Durable workflow state: exact agent run, transaction, command job, task/To-Do board, task item, checkpoint, and research project identifiers; their latest status; blockers; the next actionable item; and, for anything awaiting approval, the approval_/plan_ id with the exact call to re-issue once the user accepts it.
- Coding state: files created or modified (exact paths), key code snippets or signatures verbatim, commands run, errors seen and how they were fixed.
- Verification & evidence: tests, builds, exit status, hashes, transaction receipts, review/diff paths, and what remains unverified.
- Research findings: facts, numbers, disagreements, and findings, each tied to exact source IDs and URLs.
- Source ledger: preserve every task-relevant source_* identifier, title, URL, fetched timestamp/hash when present, and stored content/report path. Distinguish fetched source evidence from search-result snippets.
- Current state: what is already done and working.
- Next steps: what remains to do or was about to happen.

Preserve exact identifiers, file paths, code, numbers, and URLs verbatim — never paraphrase them. In particular, never drop transaction IDs, run IDs, job IDs, todo_/item_/checkpoint_ IDs, research_/query_/source_ IDs, approval_/plan_ IDs, SHA-256 hashes, artifact paths, report paths, or retention.facts from an agentic-workspace/v1 tool result. Treat retention.omit_when_summarizing as permission to omit the named bulky payload, not the result's summary, facts, IDs, status, or artifacts. Be concise everywhere else.

Output only the summary text.

 * summarize (finding L2 / ruling R9: compaction must never hard-fail, on
 * any model — degrade to a structural digest instead of throwing). A
 * one-line marker plus the chunk's own renderForSummary rendering, bounded
 * to maxChars. Pure and byte-stable (same chunk -> same digest, forever —
 * no model call, no randomness), and protocol-aware for free: agentic tool
 * results already render compactly via renderAgenticToolResultForSummary
 * inside renderForSummary, so the digest of an agentic chunk isn't a raw
 * JSON dump. Never calls the model — this is what handler.ts falls back to
 * when even the headroom retry (see respondForPayload) comes back empty.

content, so identical chains always regenerate the same prompt/summary.
